title: Streams and substructure: can a fast dark-matter stream produce the 248 keV event without a low-energy population?
question: Can a cold stream (Galactic speed v_s, lab speed v_lab, density fraction f_s) remove the low-energy population predicted by elastic scattering, extend the inelastic reach beyond delta_max or boost the rate at delta = 350-450 keV, and do known substructures (Sagittarius, S1/S2, Gaia-Enceladus, shards) help?
headline_result: No stream removes the elastic O1 low-energy population (N_lo = 1182 per 200-270 keV event, fixed by the shell-model response; SHM 2569; x2.2 reduction for every operator) and bound streams cannot raise delta_max(248 keV, 1 TeV) = 387 keV (v_lab <= 810 km/s), but a retrograde stream within 15 km/s of v_esc with f_s = 1% boosts the delta = 380 keV inelastic rate x35-51 (v_esc-truncated); delta >~ 410 keV needs unbound dark matter; known substructures have delta_max <= 194 keV
model_or_mechanism: composite halo (1-f_s) Baxter-SHM + f_s Gaussian stream (sigma 20 km/s), analytic Earth-frame eta and exact axisymmetric v_esc-truncated stream integral, WimPyDD O1 per-stream kernels, P007 Higgsino coupling, 1 TeV, 16 June
confidence: high for kinematics, N_lo and the escape-velocity ceiling (analytic, validated against WimPyDD); medium for stream-tail rates (dispersion-dependent) and recalled substructure parameters
agent_tools: Read x15, Bash x16, Write x5, Edit x19, Skill x1 (dataviz)
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1; pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; WimPyDD 2.0.4 (diff_rate per-stream kernels, v_earth_sun, streamed_halo_function for validation); common/lzcommon.py
